headline: Lenovo confirms Legion Go issues after BIOS V42 update bricked some devices
summary: Lenovo acknowledges that some Legion Go handhelds experienced blank screens during BIOS V42 installation, which was removed from their support site.
details: Lenovo has confirmed that some Legion Go devices encountered blank screens during the installation of BIOS version V42. This update was not distributed via Windows Update or Legion Space and has since been removed from the company's support website.
The issue primarily affected original Legion Go 8APU1 models that downloaded BIOS V42 (N3CN42WW) directly from Lenovo's site. Users who successfully updated should not need further action.

For devices that froze during installation, Lenovo advises pressing and holding the power button for approximately 10 seconds, waiting a minute, then powering on again. If this fails, customers should contact Lenovo Support.

An unconfirmed post by a Lenovo employee on forums suggested that devices bricked by the BIOS update should be repaired free of charge, even out of warranty, depending on local laws. Lenovo has not officially confirmed this stance.

The company is still investigating the root cause, with some teams able to reproduce the issue and others not. It's suspected the problem might be related to specific components in certain manufacturing batches or particular circumstances during installation.
